correctness.rationale: Direct substitution into all four equilibrium equations yields a bijection with physical roots 0<z<1 of a degree-at-most-four scalar Q. The \(R\le1\) contradiction uses the strict inequality \(N<a(S+I)\) from the positive vector balance. For \(R>1\) the exact endpoint signs are opposite, excluding four distinct roots. A fully exact positive-delay witness gives three physical and one nonphysical interval root, so the quartic roots are simple and persist under parameter perturbation. Actual included checker verifies the nonstandard elimination identities, residual equations and rational interval signs. This does not prove dynamical stability.

originality.rationale: The published 2023 quartic is known, and the 2016 no-delay source already mentions potential three algebraic roots; these facts are not presented as original. The new mathematically sharper contribution is the maximum three *feasible* positive coexistence equilibria for every positive-delay parameter, a proof of exclusion for R0<=1, a completely rationally certified exact example with two nonzero delays attaining three, and persistence on an open parameter region. Direct comparison of the cited statements gives no implication covering that package. Literature access and semantic search remain incomplete and are explicit risks.

value.rationale: The parent work establishes only conditional uniqueness and analyzes stability on a single branch, and an earlier related source leaves root multiplicity open. A sharp and attained count of physically admissible coexistence equilibria across all positive delays is a natural unresolved structural classification fact. The exact witness occupies an open region and resolves whether the additional algebraic roots can be jointly feasible; it is not a mere table recomputation or an arbitrary small parameter slice. It is relevant to mapping equilibrium bifurcation possibilities without promising stability or ecological calibration.
